questions.question: Which of the following statements best defines a seed in agriculture?

options.a: A seed is the only method of plant propagation.
options.b: A seed is a unit of propagation that can be either a zygotic seed or a vegetative propagule.
options.c: A seed is any part of the plant that can regenerate into a new plant.
options.d: A seed is a storage organ that does not contribute to plant propagation.
options.e: A seed is a reproductive structure that only develops through asexual propagation.

questions.explanation: Agriculturally seed is the unit of propagation and can be any part of the plant (zygotic seed or vegetative propagules) which has the capability to regenerate into a new plant.[cite: 11]

questions.question: Which of the following crops is propagated by seeds?
questions.explanation: By seeds- cereals, millets, pulses etc. Stem cutting- sugarcane & the stem cuttings of sugarcane is called as setts. Rooted slips- Napier grass, para grass, guinea grass. Tubers- potato. Chromes- onion, garlic.[cite: 11]

questions.question: The stem cuttings of sugarcane used for propagation are called
questions.explanation: Stem cutting- sugarcane & the stem cuttings of sugarcane is called as setts.[cite: 11]

questions.question: Which of the following is propagated through rooted slips?
questions.explanation: Rooted slips (rooted slips are basal two or three internodes of the stem with a few roots)- Napier grass, para grass, guinea grass.[cite: 11]

questions.question: Potato is propagated through which plant part?
questions.explanation: Tubers- potato. Grafting, budding, & layering are used to propagated horticultural crops.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What does seed vigour refer to?

options.a: The ability of a seed to germinate under laboratory conditions
options.b: The total attributes that contribute to an effective plant stand in the field
options.c: The genetic purity of a seed
options.d: The size and weight of a seed

questions.explanation: The seed vigour refers to the sum total of all the attributes that gives effective plant stand in the field.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What should be the following attributes for selecting seeds for the maintaining optimum seed population?

options.a: Seed should be free from mixture of any seed
options.b: Seed should have high germination rate
options.c: Seed should be free from any infestation
options.d: Seed should have good seed vigour

questions.explanation: They should belong to the proper variety or strain... free from mixtures... mature and well developed... high germinating capacity... free from pest and diseases... germinate rapidly and uniformly... emergence should be prompt and early vegetative growth should be vigorous.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of nucleus seed in seed production?

options.a: To produce hybrid seeds directly for commercial farming
options.b: To serve as the initial seed for purifying and maintaining a variety
options.c: To be directly sold to farmers for cultivation
options.d: To improve soil fertility through nitrogen fixation

questions.explanation: Nucleus seed is the initial seed obtained from the selected individual plant of a particular variety or a parental line for the purpose of purifying and maintaining that variety or parental line by the breeder for further multiplication.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What is the purity percentage of nucleus seed?
questions.explanation: Nucleus seeds have 100% purity percentage.[cite: 11]

questions.question: Nucleus seeds are used to produce ___ seeds
questions.explanation: Nucleus seed are used to produce breeder seed and forms the basis of total seed production.[cite: 11]

questions.question: A seed is considered to have good vigour if its germination percentage is at least ___
questions.explanation: Low vigour seed may not be able to with stand unfavourable conditions. more the 85% seed germination is considered as good seed vigour.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What is the colour tag used for Truthfully Labelled Seeds?
questions.explanation: Truthfully labelled seed is also a type of seed that is not certified but the labelling is done to indicate its quality or standard in a truthful manner. The colour tag of this type of seed is opal green with size of colour tag 15x10 cm.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What is the colour tag used for the breeder's seed?
questions.explanation: Breeder seed tags in buff colour or Golden Yellow and are signed by the concerned plant breeder and tagged to the breeder seed bags and size of tag is 12x6 cm.[cite: 11]

questions.question: Breeder seed is the progeny of which type of seed?
questions.explanation: Nucleus seed are used to produce breeder seed and forms the basis of total seed production.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What is the genetic purity percentage of breeder seed?
questions.explanation: Breeder seed produced should meet all prescribed standards viz. genetic purity (99.9% or more), physical purity (98% or more) Germination (as per crop) moisture content (less than 12%).[cite: 11]

questions.question: The progeny of breeder's seed is ___?
questions.explanation: Breeders seed serves as a source for the production of foundation seed.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What is the genetic purity percentage of foundation seed?
questions.explanation: Foundation seed: It is 99.5% genetically pure seed. Colour tag of foundation seed is white.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What is the Colour tag used for the foundation seed?
questions.explanation: Foundation seed: It is 99.5% genetically pure seed. Colour tag of foundation seed is white.[cite: 11]

questions.question: Foundation seed is the progeny of which seed?
questions.explanation: Foundation seed: It is the progeny of breeder seed produced on the farms of State Agriculture Universities/Other government farms and State Seed Corporations.[cite: 11]

questions.question: Which of the following is the progeny of foundation seed?
questions.explanation: Certified seed: It is the progeny of foundation seed produced by registered seed growers under the supervision of seed certification agencies to maintain the seed quality as per minimum seed certification standards.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What is the genetic purity percentage of certified seed?
questions.explanation: Certified seed: It is 99% genetically pure seed. Colour tag of certified seed is blue, azar blue.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What is the colour tag for the certified seed?
questions.explanation: Certified seed: It is 99% genetically pure seed. Colour tag of certified seed is blue, azar blue.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What is the primary source for producing registered seeds?
questions.explanation: Registered seed shall be the progeny of foundation seed that is so handled as to maintain its genetic identity and purity according to standard specified for the particular crop being certified.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What is the tag color used for registered seeds in seed certification programs?
questions.explanation: Registered seed: A purple colour certificate is issued for this category of seed. These seed do not form the parts of further seed production as these seeds are only maintained for their genetic purity.[cite: 11]

questions.question: Why may early or delayed sowing of crops not be advantageous?

options.b: It causes inefficient utilization of resources
options.c: It increases pest and weed incidence

questions.explanation: Early sowing and delayed sowing of crops may not be advantageous because of the following reasons: Gives lower yield, No efficient utilization of resources, More pest and weed incidence, Reduced flowering.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What should be the optimum depth of sowing for very small seeds like tobacco?
questions.explanation: Depth of sowing is very important aspect for establishing a good crop stand... Thumb rule for seed sow depth is the depth should be 3 to 4 times of seed diameter. Optimum depth for most of the field crop is 3 to 5 cm. Small seeds like pearl millet, gingerly, or millets sown at 2 to 3cm depth. Very small seed like tobacco sown at 1 cm depth.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What should be the optimum depth of sowing for most of field crops?
questions.explanation: Optimum depth for most of the field crop is 3 to 5 cm.[cite: 11]

questions.question: Which of the following is are the methods of sowing seeds?
questions.explanation: Methods of Sowing a Seed: Broadcasting, Drilling, Planting, Transplanting.[cite: 11]

questions.question: Dry sowing is adopted in clayey soil where seeds are sown in dry soil before ___ days of onset of rainfall.
questions.explanation: Dry sowing- Adopted in clayey soil where sowing operations are difficult to carry out after rainfall or irrigation so seeds are sown is dry soil before 7 to 10 days of anticipation of rainfall.[cite: 11]

questions.question: Which of the following methods is least effective in breaking dormancy caused by physiological inhibitors within the seed?
questions.explanation: Scarification - Involves physically damaging the seed coat (e.g., using sandpaper, acid, or hot water). It is effective for hard-seeded species but does not address physiological inhibitors inside the seed.[cite: 11]

questions.question: Which chemical is most commonly used for breaking physiological dormancy by mimicking plant hormones?
questions.explanation: GA3 is a plant hormone that promotes seed germination by stimulating enzyme production, breaking dormancy, and promoting cell elongation.[cite: 11]

questions.question: Which of the following method is/ are used to break the dormancy in seeds?
questions.explanation: Methods to break seed dormancy: a. Scarification b. Hot Water Treatment c. Acid Treatment d. Leaching- e. Hormonal Treatment f. Priming- g. Improvement in nutrition h. Chemical Treatment.[cite: 11]

questions.question: Which of the following chemicals are used to treat seed for better germination?
questions.explanation: Chemical Treatment- Thiourea is used to stimulate germination in some kinds of dormant seeds... Similarly, potassium nitrate and sodium hypochlorite also stimulate seed germination in many plants species.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What is the maximum financial assistance provided to SC/ST farmers for procuring a 20 qtl. seed storage bin?
questions.explanation: Assistance @ 33% subject to a maximum of Rs.3000/- for SC/ST farmers and @ 25% subject to maximum of Rs.2000 for other farmers for procuring seeds storage bin of 20 qtl. capacity.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What percentage of assistance is provided to SC/ST farmers for procuring a 20 qtl. seed storage bin?
questions.explanation: Assistance @ 33% subject to a maximum of Rs.3000/- for SC/ST farmers and @ 25% subject to maximum of Rs.2000 for other farmers for procuring seeds storage bin of 20 qtl. capacity.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What is the maximum financial assistance provided to other farmers for procuring a 20 qtl. seed storage bin?
questions.explanation: Assistance @ 33% subject to a maximum of Rs.3000/- for SC/ST farmers and @ 25% subject to maximum of Rs.2000 for other farmers for procuring seeds storage bin of 20 qtl. capacity.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What percentage of assistance is provided to other farmers for making a 10 qtl. seed storage bin under the Seed Village Scheme?
questions.explanation: Assistance @ 33% subject to maximum of Rs.1500/- to SC/ST farmers and @ 25% subject to maximum of Rs.1000/- for other farmers for making seeds storage bin of 10 qtl. capacity in the seed villages where seed village scheme is being implemented.[cite: 11]

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the Seed Village Programme (Beej Gram Yojana)?

options.b: Upgrading the quality of farmer's saved seeds

questions.explanation: Seed Village Programme (Beej Gram Yojana) Launched: 2014-15 Purpose: To upgrade the quality of farmer's saved seeds.[cite: 11]

questions.question: In which year was the Seed Village Programme (Beej Gram Yojana) launched?
questions.explanation: Seed Village Programme (Beej Gram Yojana) Launched: 2014-15 Purpose: To upgrade the quality of farmer's saved seeds.[cite: 11]
